Create cell communities using Leiden community detection

Source: R/create_communities.R
create_communities.Rd

Assigns cells in a SingleCellExperiment object to communities using the Leiden algorithm at a single chosen resolution. Community assignments are added to colData(sce) and a per-community summary table is returned alongside the updated object. Use test_resolution first to identify a suitable resolution.

Usage

create_communities(
  sce,
  graph.name = "RNA_snn",
  resolution = 0.5,
  min_cells = 5,
  feature.col = "nFeature_RNA",
  count.col = "nCount_RNA"
)

Arguments

sce

A SingleCellExperiment object. The object must contain a pre-computed nearest-neighbour graph stored in metadata(sce)$graphs under the name given by graph.name. See the Graph preparation section below for how to build and store the graph

graph.name

A character string giving the name of the graph to retrieve from metadata(sce)$graphs. Defaults to "RNA_snn".

resolution

A single numeric value controlling the granularity of Leiden clustering. Higher values produce more, smaller communities. Use test_resolution to explore candidate values before committing to one. Defaults to 0.5.

min_cells

A positive integer. Communities with fewer than this many cells are considered too small; their cells are reassigned to the nearest valid community. If all communities fall below this threshold the function stops with an informative error. Defaults to 5.

feature.col

A character string giving the name of the colData(sce) column holding the number of detected features (genes) per cell. Defaults to "nFeature_RNA", the Seurat convention. Set this if your object uses a different column name (e.g. "detected", as produced by scuttle::perCellQCMetrics). If the column is not found, mean_detected is returned as NA with a warning.

count.col

A character string giving the name of the colData(sce) column holding total counts per cell. Defaults to "nCount_RNA", the Seurat convention. Set this if your object uses a different column name (e.g. "sum", as produced by scuttle::perCellQCMetrics). If the column is not found, mean_total_counts is returned as NA with a warning.

Value

A named list with two elements:

sce

The input SingleCellExperiment object with a new community_id column added to colData.

communities_summary

A data.frame with one row per community containing:

community_id

Community identifier.

n_cells

Number of cells in the community.

mean_detected

Mean number of detected features per cell, taken from the feature.col column of colData.

mean_total_counts

Mean total counts per cell, taken from the count.col column of colData.

Details

Graph preparation:

This function does not build the nearest-neighbour graph itself. The graph must be computed and stored in metadata(sce)$graphs before calling this function. Two workflows are supported:

1. From scratch with scran:


library(scran)

# Build a shared nearest-neighbour graph on the PCA embedding
g <- scran::buildSNNGraph(sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)

# Store it under the name this function will look for
metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g

2. From an existing Seurat object:


library(Seurat)

# Convert to SCE first
sce <- as.SingleCellExperiment(seurat_obj)

# Extract the adjacency matrix from the Seurat object, convert to igraph,
# and store in the SCE metadata
g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  seurat_obj@graphs[["RNA_snn"]],
  mode     = "max",
  weighted = TRUE
)
metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g

The value passed to graph.name must match the key used when storing the graph in metadata(sce)$graphs.

See also

test_resolution to evaluate resolution choices before running this function

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(scran)

# Build and store the graph
g <- scran::buildSNNGraph(sce, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)
metadata(sce)$graphs[["RNA_snn"]] <- g

# Optionally explore resolutions first
test_resolution(sce, resolutions = c(0.5, 1, 2.5, 5))

# Create communities at the chosen resolution
out <- create_communities(sce, resolution = 1)
sce <- out$sce
summary_df <- out$communities_summary

# If sce was built with scuttle::perCellQCMetrics() rather than Seurat,
# specify the matching column names
out <- create_communities(sce, resolution = 1,
                           feature.col = "detected",
                           count.col = "sum")
} # }
